trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is a receipt, not a task: it appears once the other 54 trophies are on your profile. Nothing on this list is online, so the whole thing can be done solo in one save. The order in our roadmap is built to protect the chapter-bound work first, then sweep collectibles and activities, and leave 100% for last because its in-game audit is the final check. Keep a manual save before the final mission so a missed stranger strand or partner run is a reload away, not a new playthrough.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission and the game's tutorial in disguise: it walks you through driving, cover shooting and the first taste of the wanted system. Finish it and the bronze is yours; there is no branch that can fail it permanently. Play the mission rather than skipping its prompts, because the mechanics it teaches are the same ones behind Stunts, Combat Focus and the robbery trophies later on. It sits first on the roadmap only because everything else unlocks behind it.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 closes with the last mission of the first act, and the trophy drops on the closing cutscene rather than on any single job. It cannot be missed while you keep playing the story, and it cannot be failed: if the counter has not appeared, the chapter's final mission is still open somewhere on the map. Treat the chapter break as a checkpoint: finish any stranger marker that has already appeared before you move on, because new strands are introduced chapter by chapter.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: The second chapter trophy lands when the Chapter 2 story thread ends, and it is unmissable on a normal playthrough. Chapter 2 is where the game starts handing you the property and business systems that the money trophies depend on, so it is worth doing the chapter's side offers before the finale rather than racing the main path. If you are replaying for cleanup, the chapter counter is a better progress marker than the mission list: it only moves when the act is genuinely closed.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Chapter 3 ends with the trophy, and by then most of the map and the partner systems are open. This is the natural point to clear the partner-dependent bronze trophies and any stranger strand you have been saving, because the last chapter tightens the story's grip on free roam. The trophy itself has no missable window: finish the chapter's last mission and it appears. Use the chapter break as a cleanup gate rather than pushing straight into Chapter 4.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: The Chapter 4 trophy is the last of the four act markers and the strongest signal that the endgame is next. It is unmissable, but it also marks the edge of the missable window for the side strands and partner moments: once Chapter 4's story thread closes, the game moves toward the final mission and those offers stop. Save in a new slot before completing the chapter's last job, then spend that save on any cleanup the roadmap still lists.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The final mission carries the story's gold and the credits. It is the point of no return in practice, so the roadmap puts every chapter-bound trophy ahead of it: stranger finales, the partner wanted-level runs and the choice-driven bronze all have to be done before you start it. Keep a manual save immediately before launching the mission; the mission itself can be replayed from the pause menu if you want a cleaner run, but a pre-mission save is the safer habit.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is one of the named story missions, and the trophy is simply its completion flag. It sits early in the story run and doubles as an introduction to the game's mission structure: a drive, a conversation, and a short burst of action. There is no missable window and no medal requirement, so play it at your own pace. If you are auditing a save, the mission replay menu lists it by name, which makes it easy to confirm you have not skipped it.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is the story's first full heist and the mission that teaches the crew-and-escape loop behind the bank vault trophy. Finish it for the bronze; the mission is on the main path, so it cannot be locked out. Watch how the game handles the alarm and the escape vehicle: the same pattern returns in the free-roam robberies, and the heist's checkpoint structure makes it a comfortable place to practise losing a wanted level cleanly.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a mid-story mission and its bronze is a straight completion flag. It is unmissable, but it is worth noting where it falls: the mission sits in the stretch where the game starts offering the stranger strands and partner activities, so it is a good moment to break off and clear whatever markers have appeared. The trophy has no medal or difficulty requirement, so a messy completion still counts.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is one of the story's named missions and its trophy is the completion flag. It lands in the back half of the campaign, where the missions get longer and the checkpoints sparser, so budget a clean attempt rather than a speedrun. Nothing about it is missable and no medal is required. If you are chasing the gold for the final mission later, this is a reasonable place to shake off the rust before the endgame.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is the story mission set around the airport, and it is also the best rehearsal for the free-roam VCIA trophy. Complete it for the bronze, and pay attention to how the mission routes you through the terminal and the airfield: the unrestricted departure trophy asks you to do something similar without a mission holding your hand. The mission itself is on the main path and cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a late-story mission, and its bronze comes with the completion flag. It is unmissable and has no medal requirement, but it sits close enough to the finale that the chapter-bound cleanup should already be done. If you are following the roadmap, this mission is the last natural pause before the endgame: finish any open stranger strand, then take the final mission with a clear save.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: 100% is the long gold: the pause-menu completion audit counts story, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and challenges, and it does not care in what order you did them. Work from that audit rather than from memory, and leave it for last so every other trophy's progress feeds it. The last few percent are almost always a single unplayed activity type or one unvisited area; the audit names the category, which is why our roadmap ends here.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Stunts are the series' jump-and-roll moves: a committed hop, a clean landing, and a chained follow-up. The count is the grind, not the difficulty, so pick a stretch of beach or highway with open run-up and repeat short chains rather than hunting exotic spots. The stats page tracks the total, and the counter only moves on a landed stunt, so a bail costs you nothing but time. Put on a fast, stable car and treat it as a rhythm exercise.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: The description fixes the shape of this one: nine activity types, each played once, and finishing is enough. Open the map's activity filter and work down the list rather than guessing: shooting range, drone race, street race, fishing, arcade, bowling and the rest each count as their own type. A single round of each is all it takes, so this is the cheapest bronze on the activity list and a natural first stop when you start the cleanup sweep.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold on all 42 Shooting Range challenges is the list's purest skill check. The range scores accuracy and time together, so the winning habit is a slow first pass to learn each stage's target order, then a fast one once you know where the plates appear. Do this after the story, with the weapon upgrades you have earned, and start with the pistol challenges: they teach the scoring rhythm before the long-range and moving-target stages raise the price of a miss.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: There are 14 drone-race locations and the trophy wants a win at each one, not a finish. The races are short, so a bad run is cheaper to restart than to salvage; learn the first two gates, then commit to a line. Do them district by district and tick the location off in the map filter. The drone's handling rewards small corrections, so resist holding full stick through the turns.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty different race wins: repeating one circuit will not move the counter, so the map's race markers are the real checklist. Street races are the quickest route, and a fully upgraded car turns most of them into a formality. Win one per location, note the ones you have won, and save the long highway events for last when your driving is warm. The trophy counts wins, not podiums, so a second place is a retry.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is one of the game's activity characters, and the challenge is a head-to-head fishing contest rather than a solo grind. Learn the cast-and-reel timing on ordinary fish first: the trophy rewards a clean hook-set and steady tension, not button mashing. Once you can land a few without snapping the line, take Cal on. If you lose, the challenge can be repeated, so there is no missable window here.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Any in-world arcade cabinet will do, and the requirement is completion, not a high score. Pick the shortest cabinet you can find and use continues liberally; the trophy does not care how many credits it took. Arcades are indoor locations, so this pairs naturally with the shop-spending and bowling trophies on the same trip. If a cabinet offers a two-player mode, a second controller is not needed: solo play counts.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.

missable.why: Andy's line is a stranger strand, and strand offers stop once the story reaches its final mission.
missable.order: Finish Andy's markers as soon as the last one appears; do not leave it for the endgame.

trophies.guide: Andy's strand is a multi-mission stranger line, and the trophy is its final mission rather than the first meeting. Run the markers as they appear instead of saving the strand for the endgame: the game stops offering stranger work once the final mission is live, which is why our roadmap puts every strand in stage 2. Andy's jobs are short, so the whole line is an evening's work if you do it in one sitting.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.

missable.why: Kenton's strand is chapter-bound side content; its markers stop after the story's final mission.
missable.order: Clear Kenton's line during Chapters 2 to 4, before you start the finale.

trophies.guide: Kenton's line is one of the named stranger strands, and its last mission is the trophy. The strand opens in the middle chapters, so the practical order is to finish it as soon as the final marker shows rather than waiting for a clean sweep. There is no medal requirement and no branch: complete the last job and the bronze appears. If the marker has gone quiet, check whether you have already started the endgame.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.

missable.why: Billy's strand is side content with a story-bound cutoff; the markers stop after the final mission.
missable.order: Do Billy's strand before Chapter 4's last mission; earlier is safer.

trophies.guide: Billy's strand is a stranger line with a definitive final mission, and the trophy is that mission. The line is easy to postpone because its markers sit away from the main path, which is exactly how players lose it: once the endgame starts, the offers dry up. Treat the first Billy marker as a reminder to finish the whole line, and use a manual save before Chapter 4's finale as insurance.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.

missable.why: The description asks for eight complete strands; strand offers end with the story, so a strand left open is lost.
missable.order: Track every stranger marker you meet; finish eight lines before the finale.

trophies.guide: The silver wants eight complete strands, not eight strangers met. The named finales in this list (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of them, and Bret's and Cal's activity lines are the obvious next stops, so a full map sweep will clear the bar. Keep a simple tally: a strand counts when its final mission is done. This is the trophy that most rewards doing side content between chapters instead of after the credits.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.

missable.why: Randy's strand is one of the side lines that closes when the story's final mission begins.
missable.order: Finish Randy's markers in stage 2, alongside the other strands.

trophies.guide: Randy's line is a stranger strand whose final job carries the bronze. It runs alongside the other named strands, so the efficient plan is to sweep all of them in one pass: the markers cluster, and finishing them together is faster than travelling back and forth. Complete the final mission and the trophy is yours; there is no alternative ending to worry about. The only way to lose it is to start the finale with the strand unfinished.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.

missable.why: Tyrone's strand is side content that stops being offered after the story's final mission.
missable.order: Clear Tyrone's line before the point of no return; do not save it for 100% cleanup.

trophies.guide: Tyrone's strand ends in a named final mission and the bronze comes with it. Like the other strands it is chapter-bound, so the roadmap treats it as stage 2 work: finish the line while the story is still running, and do not assume the endgame will let you come back. The jobs themselves are straightforward; the risk is entirely in the timing, which the missable flag on this entry is there to prevent.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eighteen meditation spots are spread across the state, and each is a short hold-button scene rather than a minigame. The map's collectible filter marks them, so the work is routing rather than skill: do them region by region and pair each cluster with the area visits for The Goodtime State. There is no missable window, and a spot can be revisited if you interrupt the animation.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret's request is for one specific animal, not any kill: the trophy is tied to the unique hunt his strand sets up. Take the hunting rifle rather than an automatic weapon, aim for a clean shot, and follow the tracking prompt instead of charging the area. The animal can be found again if the first attempt goes wrong, so this is not a missable trophy, but a botched shot means a long walk back to the trail.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: The card trophy counts completed sets, not loose cards: three full sets are needed, and the collectibles menu shows each set's progress. Duplicates are the enemy, so buy packs from different vendors and check which set is closest to done before spending. Card packs are a money sink, which is why this sits after the story in the roadmap: heist income makes the last few cards painless.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It is the in-game social app, and the trophy asks for a check-in at 100 different locations. It is the longest location grind on the list, so fold it into other sweeps: every meditation spot, card vendor and area visit is also a place to check in. The app marks locations you have already used, which prevents wasting a trip. No missable window, just a hundred small stops.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: The challenge list is the game's long tail: weapon-specific kills, traversal stunts, robbery variants and similar feats. Fifty of them will come naturally across a 100% run, so the efficient approach is to check the list once you have finished the story and pick the ten or so that are still open. Each challenge names its own condition, and progress is tracked per challenge rather than as a single counter.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.

missable.when: Chapters 3 to 4, before the final mission
missable.why: It needs your partner in free roam, and partner availability is story-bound.
missable.order: Do it after the partner systems unlock and before the endgame; keep a save.

trophies.guide: Build a four-star wanted level with your partner in the car, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. The mistake most players make is trying to outrun the police in the open: use alleys, tunnels and off-road cover, and keep the partner with you rather than letting them bail. Because the partner is a story-bound companion, this is flagged missable; do it while the story is still live.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.

missable.when: Chapters 3 to 4, before the final mission
missable.why: The run requires your partner and a live wanted level; both are tied to the story phase.
missable.order: Plan three nearby shops and do the run before the final mission.

trophies.guide: The condition is a chain: three shop robberies with no gap long enough for the wanted level to clear. Scout three stores within a short drive of each other, rob them in one loop, and keep moving between jobs instead of fighting the police. A fast car and a route that avoids main roads matter more than firepower. The partner must stay with you for the whole run, so this is flagged as chapter-bound.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discovering a vehicle means getting behind the wheel of a model you have not driven before; the pause-menu vehicle list marks the gaps. Races and robberies hand you a variety for free, so the trophy mostly takes care of itself until the last twenty or so. For those, work through the dealerships and the airport parking: rare models spawn where the game wants you to notice them.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is the slow-time aiming ability, and the trophy wants five kills inside one activation. Do not pop it at the first enemy: let a group gather, then activate and chain headshots from cover. A gang operation or a bank vault's guard room is the reliable setup, because the enemies come to you. If the meter runs out at four, reload the checkpoint and try again with a tighter group.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is the game's airport, and an unscheduled departure means getting airside and airborne outside the normal flight flow. Drive or walk in through the service side, reach the apron, and take a plane before the security response closes the runway. The story's VCIA Takedown mission is a useful rehearsal for the layout. Expect a wanted level; the trophy fires on the takeoff, not on a clean escape.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The Rhino is the game's tank, and the cryptic description is the whole hint: get one and deal with it. Tanks appear when the wanted level climbs high enough, so the setup is a long chase that ends with the military response. Hijacking one is cleaner than destroying it; either way, the trophy is about the encounter rather than a specific location. Bring explosives and keep moving.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: No alarm and no witness is the whole job. Scout the store in advance, take out the cameras before you cross the floor, and use a silenced weapon on any guard who sees you. The display cases are the objective; grab and leave rather than clearing the building. If the alarm trips, the trophy is done for that attempt, so restart the robbery from the map instead of fighting through it.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Five bank vaults, five escapes. Vault robberies are the multi-stage jobs: entry, vault drill, and a getaway that has to actually clear the wanted level. Do them after the story with a crew and an upgraded getaway car, and vary the banks rather than repeating one. The pause-menu stats page tracks how many vaults you have cleared, so use it as the checklist instead of memory.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks are random road events: a truck with a escort, a brief stop, and a rear door that opens to explosives. Hit it when it slows at a junction, plant a sticky bomb on the back, take the cash and leave before the responders box you in. One successful robbery and an escape is all the trophy asks; the truck does not need to be a specific one.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Leonida is split into 52 named areas, and visiting each one once is enough. The area name appears on screen when you cross into a new district, which is the confirmation to watch for. A perimeter drive plus a pass through the islands and the interior covers most of them; the map's fog and the area list show what is left. Pair the drive with WAiNK check-ins and vehicle discovery to make one trip count three times.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Nine gangs run illegal operations across the state, and the trophy wants one robbery from each gang's operation, not nine from one. The map marks operations by gang once you have met them, so keep a list and cross off the gang rather than the location. These are the same multi-stage robberies as the banks, but the resistance is gang-specific; scout first, then bring the right tools.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: A flavour trophy: find a bar with an outdoor terrace on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail and let the scene play. It is not a grind and it is not tied to a mission, so the only real requirement is the venue: the view is part of the description, which points at the beachfront terraces rather than an interior bar. Do it early, when you first reach Ocean Beach, and it becomes a free bronze on the way to something else.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: The classic style is the hint: drive a car through the showroom glass rather than walking out the door. Any vehicle showroom works, and the trophy fires on the escape, so pick one with a clean run to the street. It pairs neatly with the shop-spending trophy, since showrooms are shops too. Expect a wanted level, and do not bother being subtle about it.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Kolt & Associates runs the bowling alley, and the trophy is for finishing a game there rather than winning it. Bowling uses a timing meter: stop the moving marker at the line, then apply spin on the return. One full game is enough, so this is a ten-minute stop. It also counts toward the nine activity types, which makes it a good first pick when you start the activity sweep.

trophies.name: Personal Best

missable.when: During the partnership story beat, before the finale
missable.why: The description points at a one-time partnership moment rather than repeatable free roam.
missable.order: Play the partnership missions as they arrive; keep a save before the choice.

trophies.guide: The description is deliberately coy, but "a partnership with mass appeal" reads as a story beat about going public with a partnership rather than a skill challenge. Play the partnership missions as they arrive and take the public-facing option when the scene offers it. Because it looks like a one-time story moment, it is flagged as missable: keep a save before the beat in case the wrong choice closes it.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

missable.when: Throughout the story, before the final mission
missable.why: Story choices are one-time; the PSN counter tracks them to 500, and the endgame stops new ones.
missable.order: Take the choice prompts when they appear; do not skip story content.

trophies.guide: The trophy is about making choices, and PlayStation tracks a counter of 500 for it. That sounds enormous, but the counter moves on ordinary dialogue and mission decisions, so a full story plus side content gets there without farming. The only way to fall short is to skip the content that offers choices, which is why it is flagged for the story window. Do not replay a mission for it; just play the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

missable.when: During a story mission, before the finale
missable.why: It reads as a retry beat tied to a story mission; the chance disappears once the story is over.
missable.order: If a mission offers a retry prompt, take it rather than reloading a save.

trophies.guide: The description is a retry joke: fail once, then succeed on the second attempt. The reliable method is a short story mission where a failure is cheap: deliberately fail the objective, let the game offer its retry, then finish it cleanly. Do not reload a manual save instead, because that is a different flow. Flagged as a story-window trophy because the retry prompt is a mission feature.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

missable.when: During the story's strange encounters, before the finale
missable.why: It reads as a one-time odd encounter, the kind the story stages once and does not repeat.
missable.order: Follow unusual map markers and blue-dot encounters when they appear.

trophies.guide: A cryptic bronze for witnessing something strange, in the series' tradition of hidden oddities. The practical approach is to follow the map's unusual markers and the blue-dot encounters when they appear, and to let the scene play out rather than driving away. It reads as a one-time story-adjacent event, so it is flagged: if something weird starts, stay for the whole thing.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by means a melee attack from a moving vehicle: pull alongside a pedestrian, swing, and knock them down. A quiet side street is the safest stage for it, and the trophy fires on the hit rather than on the aftermath. Expect a wanted level, so have an escape route. It is a silly one-off and does not need a specific vehicle.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills come from robberies, and laundering them through your contacts is how they become clean money. The trophy is cumulative: $250,000 in total, not in one drop. Run your robbery proceeds through the contact's business after each job rather than hoarding them, and check the laundering screen's running total. It pairs with the shop-spending trophy: clean money is what you spend.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Cumulative spending across shops, so there is no single purchase to save for: weapons, clothes, car upgrades and property all count. The efficient route is to spend as you go rather than grinding one shopping trip at the end. If you are short, upgrade a couple of cars and buy the weapons you will use for the shooting range; the money still counts and the gear helps other trophies.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: All eight garage properties have to be bought, and the property map lists them with prices. The cheap ones come first, but the total is the point, so plan the purchases around heist income rather than draining your account early. Garages also give you somewhere to store the rare vehicles you find for the discovery trophy, which makes this a useful investment rather than a pure expense.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Scooter Bros is the vehicle app, and registration is a separate action from simply driving a car. Register ten different vehicles through the app; the menu shows which ones are already linked, so there is no guesswork. This overlaps with the 100-vehicle discovery trophy, but it is not the same counter: a car can be discovered without being registered. Do the registrations in one session once you own a few vehicles.
